sections.label: GST refund on 18 Government fees
sections.summary: MOF announced on 14 February 2024 that GST charged on 18 Government fees across six agencies would be refunded, as these regulatory fees should not have been charged GST.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minster for Finance)
sentences.text: As Members are aware, Ministry of Finance (MOF) announced on 14 February 2024 that GST charged on 18 Government fees across six agencies would be refunded.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minster for Finance)
sentences.text: This arose from an internal review of regulatory and ancillary fees that charge GST, where we discovered that GST should not have been charged on these 18 fees, as they are regulatory in nature.

sections.label: Review of remaining Government fees
sections.summary: MOF is reviewing more than 1,700 remaining regulatory and ancillary Government fees that do not charge GST.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minster for Finance)
sentences.text: We are now working with agencies on the remaining regulatory and ancillary fees, which do not charge GST.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minster for Finance)
sentences.text: There are in total more than 1,700 such Government fees, which MOF is in the midst of reviewing.

sections.label: GST absorption and fee freeze
sections.summary: The Government will absorb GST on fees that must charge GST and freeze these fees until end-2025, with agencies reviewing possible reductions.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minster for Finance)
sentences.text: For this third category of fees where GST has to be charged, the Government will help to minimise the impact on the public.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minster for Finance)
sentences.text: We will absorb the GST on these fees in the first instance and impose a freeze on these fees until end-2025.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minster for Finance)
sentences.text: MOF has separately asked the agencies involved to review their fees and charges and to consider ways where they can streamline processes or reduce costs.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minster for Finance)
sentences.text: We will work closely with agencies on this, to review if the above-mentioned fees may be reduced or even removed.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minster for Finance)
sentences.text: If there are unavoidable cost increases, then agencies would have to raise their fees.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minster for Finance)
sentences.text: But they will do so only after end-2025 and will ensure that any increases are phased-in gradually, taking into consideration the impact on affected stakeholders.

sections.label: Validation clause and excluded supplies
sections.summary: Clause 4 validates GST purportedly imposed before the new Act's publication, bars legal proceedings from 7 March 2024, and a Schedule lists excluded supplies including the 18 types.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Under clause 4 of the Bill, or the validation clause, every sum purportedly imposed as GST, before the date of publication of the new Act, on any supply made in connection with the performance of a regulatory function by a public agency, is deemed to be and always to have been, validly imposed.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Accordingly, clause 4 goes on to say that no legal proceedings may be instituted on or after 7 March 2024 in respect of the imposition of any of these taxes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The provision is then accompanied by a Schedule, which sets out a list of supplies to which clause 4, the validation clause, does not apply.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This list includes details of the 18 different types of supplies which relate to the sums of GST wrongfully collected by Government agencies as announced by MOF on 14 February.
